1	---
2	layout: default
3	title : "Setoid.Homomorphisms.Kernels module (Agda Universal Algebra Library)"
4	date : "2021-09-13"
5	author: "agda-algebras development team"
6	---
7	
8	#### Kernels of Homomorphisms
9	
10	This is the [Setoid.Homomorphisms.Kernels][] module of the [Agda Universal Algebra Library][].
11	
12	The **kernel** of a homomorphism `h : hom 𝑨 𝑩` is the binary relation on the
13	carrier of `𝑨` that relates `a₀` and `a₁` when `h a₀` and `h a₁` are equal in `𝑩`.
14	
15	It is an equivalence relation because it is the pullback of one along `h`, which is
16	`kerRelOfEquiv`{.AgdaFunction} of [Overture.Relations][]; what this module adds is
17	that it is also compatible with the basic operations, hence a congruence, so that
18	the quotient by the kernel is again an algebra.
19	
20	`HomKerComp`{.AgdaFunction} is the compatibility proof, `kercon`{.AgdaFunction} is
21	the congruence, and `kerquo`{.AgdaFunction}, also written `ker[ 𝑨 ⇒ 𝑩 ] h`, is the
22	quotient.
23	
24	This module also supplies the homomorphisms that go with a quotient:
25	
26	+  `πepi`{.AgdaFunction} is the canonical projection of `𝑨` onto `𝑨 ╱ θ`, for any
27	   congruence `θ`, presented as an epimorphism;
28	+  `πhom`{.AgdaFunction} is its homomorphism reduct;
29	+  `πker`{.AgdaFunction} is the special case that projects onto a kernel quotient;
30	+  `ker-in-con`{.AgdaFunction} says the kernel of `πhom θ` is contained in `θ`.
31	
32	Together with the congruences of [Setoid.Congruences][], these are the components
33	with which the first homomorphism theorem of [Setoid.Homomorphisms.Noether][] is
34	stated.
35	
36	<!--
37	```agda
38	{-# OPTIONS --cubical-compatible --exact-split --safe #-}
39	
40	module Setoid.Homomorphisms.Kernels where
41	
42	-- Imports from Agda and the Agda Standard Library ------------------------------------------
43	open  import Data.Product                           using ( _,_ ;  proj₁ ; proj₂ )
44	open  import Function   renaming ( Func to _⟶_ )    using ( _∘_ ; id )
45	open  import Level                                  using ( Level )
46	open  import Relation.Binary                        using ( Setoid )
47	open  import Relation.Binary.PropositionalEquality  using (refl)
48	
49	-- Imports from the Agda Universal Algebra Library ------------------------------------------
50	open  import Overture                    using ( kerRel ; kerRelOfEquiv ; 𝓞 ; 𝓥 ; Signature)
51	open  import Setoid.Functions            using ( Image_∋_ )
52	open  import Setoid.Algebras             using ( Algebra ; _^_ ; 𝔻[_] )
53	open  import Setoid.Congruences          using ( _∣≈_ ; Con ; mkcon ; _╱_ ; IsCongruence )
54	open  import Setoid.Homomorphisms.Basic  using ( hom ; IsHom ; epi ; IsEpi ; epi→hom ; 𝒾𝒹 )
55	
56	private variable  α β ρᵃ ρᵇ ℓ : Level
57	
58	open _⟶_ using ( cong ) renaming ( to to _⟨$⟩_ )
59	```
60	-->
61	
62	```agda
63	module _ {𝑆 : Signature 𝓞 𝓥} {𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ}{𝑩 : Algebra β ρᵇ} ((hmap , hhom) : hom 𝑨 𝑩) where
64	  open Algebra 𝑩   using ( Interp ) renaming ( Domain to B )
65	  open Setoid B    using ( _≈_ ; sym ; trans ; isEquivalence )
66	  private h = _⟨$⟩_ hmap
67	```
68	
69	`HomKerComp` asserts that the kernel of a homomorphism is compatible with the basic operations.
70	That is, if each `(u i, v i)` belongs to the kernel, then so does the pair `((f ^ 𝑨) u , (f ^ 𝑨) v)`.
71	
72	```agda
73	  HomKerComp : 𝑨 ∣≈ kerRel _≈_ h
74	  HomKerComp f {u}{v} kuv = Goal
75	    where
76	    fhuv : (f ^ 𝑩)(h ∘ u) ≈ (f ^ 𝑩)(h ∘ v)
77	    fhuv = cong Interp (refl , kuv)
78	
79	    lem1 : h ((f ^ 𝑨) u) ≈ (f ^ 𝑩)(h ∘ u)
80	    lem1 = IsHom.compatible hhom
81	
82	    lem2 : (f ^ 𝑩) (h ∘ v) ≈ h ((f ^ 𝑨) v)
83	    lem2 = sym (IsHom.compatible hhom)
84	
85	    Goal : h ((f ^ 𝑨) u) ≈ h ((f ^ 𝑨) v)
86	    Goal = trans lem1 (trans fhuv lem2)
87	```
88	
89	The kernel of a homomorphism is a congruence of the domain, which we construct as follows.
90	
91	```agda
92	  kercon : Con 𝑨 ρᵇ
93	  kercon =  kerRel _≈_ h ,
94	            mkcon (λ x → cong hmap x)(kerRelOfEquiv isEquivalence h)(HomKerComp)
95	```
96	
97	Now that we have a congruence, we can construct the quotient relative to the kernel.
98	
99	```agda
100	  kerquo : Algebra α ρᵇ
101	  kerquo = 𝑨 ╱ kercon
102	
103	ker[_⇒_]_ :  {𝑆 : Signature 𝓞 𝓥} (𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ) (𝑩 : Algebra β ρᵇ) → hom 𝑨 𝑩 → Algebra _ _
104	ker[ 𝑨 ⇒ 𝑩 ] h = kerquo h
105	```
106	
107	
108	#### The canonical projection
109	
110	Given an algebra `𝑨` and a congruence `θ`, the *canonical projection* is a map
111	from `𝑨` onto `𝑨 ╱ θ` that is constructed, and proved epimorphic, as follows.
112	
113	```agda
114	module _ {𝑆 : Signature 𝓞 𝓥} {𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ}{𝑩 : Algebra β ρᵇ} (h : hom 𝑨 𝑩) where
115	  open IsCongruence
116	
117	  πepi : (θ : Con 𝑨 ℓ) → epi 𝑨 (𝑨 ╱ θ)
118	  πepi θ = p , pepi
119	    where
120	
121	    open Setoid 𝔻[ 𝑨 ╱ θ ]    using () renaming ( sym to ≈sym ; refl to ≈refl )
122	    open IsHom {𝑨 = (𝑨 ╱ θ)}  using ( compatible )
123	    open IsEpi
124	
125	    p : 𝔻[ 𝑨 ] ⟶ 𝔻[ 𝑨 ╱ θ ]
126	    p ⟨$⟩ x = x
127	    p .cong = reflexive (θ .proj₂)
128	
129	    pepi : IsEpi 𝑨 (𝑨 ╱ θ) p
130	    pepi .isHom .compatible = ≈sym (𝒾𝒹 .proj₂ .compatible)
131	    pepi .isSurjective {y} = Image_∋_.eq y ≈refl
132	```
133	
134	In may happen that we don't care about the surjectivity of `πepi`, in which
135	case would might prefer to work with the *homomorphic reduct* of `πepi`.
136	This is obtained by applying `epi-to-hom`, like so.
137	
138	```agda
139	  πhom : (θ : Con 𝑨 ℓ) → hom 𝑨 (𝑨 ╱ θ)
140	  πhom θ = epi→hom 𝑨 (𝑨 ╱ θ) (πepi θ)
141	```
142	
143	We combine the foregoing to define a function that takes 𝑆-algebras `𝑨` and `𝑩`,
144	and a homomorphism `h : hom 𝑨 𝑩` and returns the canonical epimorphism from `𝑨`
145	onto `𝑨 [ 𝑩 ]/ker h`. (Recall, the latter is the special notation we defined
146	above for the quotient of `𝑨` modulo the kernel of `h`.)
147	
148	```agda
149	  πker : epi 𝑨 (ker[ 𝑨 ⇒ 𝑩 ] h)
150	  πker = πepi (kercon h)
151	```
152	
153	The kernel of the canonical projection of `𝑨` onto `𝑨 / θ` is equal to `θ`,
154	but since equality of inhabitants of certain types (like `Congruence` or `Rel`)
155	can be a tricky business, we settle for proving the containment `𝑨 / θ ⊆ θ`.
156	Of the two containments, this is the easier one to prove; luckily it is also
157	the one we need later.
158	
159	```agda
160	  ker-in-con : {θ : Con 𝑨 ℓ} → ∀ {x}{y} → kercon (πhom θ) .proj₁ x y →  θ .proj₁ x y
161	  ker-in-con = id
162	```
163

---
layout: default
title : "Setoid.Homomorphisms.Kernels module (Agda Universal Algebra Library)"
date : "2021-09-13"
author: "agda-algebras development team"
---

#### Kernels of Homomorphisms

This is the [Setoid.Homomorphisms.Kernels][] module of the [Agda Universal Algebra Library][].

The **kernel** of a homomorphism `h : hom 𝑨 𝑩` is the binary relation on the
carrier of `𝑨` that relates `a₀` and `a₁` when `h a₀` and `h a₁` are equal in `𝑩`.

It is an equivalence relation because it is the pullback of one along `h`, which is
`kerRelOfEquiv`{.AgdaFunction} of [Overture.Relations][]; what this module adds is
that it is also compatible with the basic operations, hence a congruence, so that
the quotient by the kernel is again an algebra.

`HomKerComp`{.AgdaFunction} is the compatibility proof, `kercon`{.AgdaFunction} is
the congruence, and `kerquo`{.AgdaFunction}, also written `ker[ 𝑨 ⇒ 𝑩 ] h`, is the
quotient.

This module also supplies the homomorphisms that go with a quotient:

+  `πepi`{.AgdaFunction} is the canonical projection of `𝑨` onto `𝑨 ╱ θ`, for any
   congruence `θ`, presented as an epimorphism;
+  `πhom`{.AgdaFunction} is its homomorphism reduct;
+  `πker`{.AgdaFunction} is the special case that projects onto a kernel quotient;
+  `ker-in-con`{.AgdaFunction} says the kernel of `πhom θ` is contained in `θ`.

Together with the congruences of [Setoid.Congruences][], these are the components
with which the first homomorphism theorem of [Setoid.Homomorphisms.Noether][] is
stated.

<!--
```agda
{-# OPTIONS --cubical-compatible --exact-split --safe #-}

module Setoid.Homomorphisms.Kernels where

-- Imports from Agda and the Agda Standard Library ------------------------------------------
open  import Data.Product                           using ( _,_ ;  proj₁ ; proj₂ )
open  import Function   renaming ( Func to _⟶_ )    using ( _∘_ ; id )
open  import Level                                  using ( Level )
open  import Relation.Binary                        using ( Setoid )
open  import Relation.Binary.PropositionalEquality  using (refl)

-- Imports from the Agda Universal Algebra Library ------------------------------------------
open  import Overture                    using ( kerRel ; kerRelOfEquiv ; 𝓞 ; 𝓥 ; Signature)
open  import Setoid.Functions            using ( Image_∋_ )
open  import Setoid.Algebras             using ( Algebra ; _^_ ; 𝔻[_] )
open  import Setoid.Congruences          using ( _∣≈_ ; Con ; mkcon ; _╱_ ; IsCongruence )
open  import Setoid.Homomorphisms.Basic  using ( hom ; IsHom ; epi ; IsEpi ; epi→hom ; 𝒾𝒹 )

private variable  α β ρᵃ ρᵇ ℓ : Level

open _⟶_ using ( cong ) renaming ( to to _⟨$⟩_ )
```
-->

```agda
module _ {𝑆 : Signature 𝓞 𝓥} {𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ}{𝑩 : Algebra β ρᵇ} ((hmap , hhom) : hom 𝑨 𝑩) where
  open Algebra 𝑩   using ( Interp ) renaming ( Domain to B )
  open Setoid B    using ( _≈_ ; sym ; trans ; isEquivalence )
  private h = _⟨$⟩_ hmap
```

`HomKerComp` asserts that the kernel of a homomorphism is compatible with the basic operations.
That is, if each `(u i, v i)` belongs to the kernel, then so does the pair `((f ^ 𝑨) u , (f ^ 𝑨) v)`.

```agda
  HomKerComp : 𝑨 ∣≈ kerRel _≈_ h
  HomKerComp f {u}{v} kuv = Goal
    where
    fhuv : (f ^ 𝑩)(h ∘ u) ≈ (f ^ 𝑩)(h ∘ v)
    fhuv = cong Interp (refl , kuv)

    lem1 : h ((f ^ 𝑨) u) ≈ (f ^ 𝑩)(h ∘ u)
    lem1 = IsHom.compatible hhom

    lem2 : (f ^ 𝑩) (h ∘ v) ≈ h ((f ^ 𝑨) v)
    lem2 = sym (IsHom.compatible hhom)

    Goal : h ((f ^ 𝑨) u) ≈ h ((f ^ 𝑨) v)
    Goal = trans lem1 (trans fhuv lem2)
```

The kernel of a homomorphism is a congruence of the domain, which we construct as follows.

```agda
  kercon : Con 𝑨 ρᵇ
  kercon =  kerRel _≈_ h ,
            mkcon (λ x → cong hmap x)(kerRelOfEquiv isEquivalence h)(HomKerComp)
```

Now that we have a congruence, we can construct the quotient relative to the kernel.

```agda
  kerquo : Algebra α ρᵇ
  kerquo = 𝑨 ╱ kercon

ker[_⇒_]_ :  {𝑆 : Signature 𝓞 𝓥} (𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ) (𝑩 : Algebra β ρᵇ) → hom 𝑨 𝑩 → Algebra _ _
ker[ 𝑨 ⇒ 𝑩 ] h = kerquo h
```


#### The canonical projection

Given an algebra `𝑨` and a congruence `θ`, the *canonical projection* is a map
from `𝑨` onto `𝑨 ╱ θ` that is constructed, and proved epimorphic, as follows.

```agda
module _ {𝑆 : Signature 𝓞 𝓥} {𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ}{𝑩 : Algebra β ρᵇ} (h : hom 𝑨 𝑩) where
  open IsCongruence

  πepi : (θ : Con 𝑨 ℓ) → epi 𝑨 (𝑨 ╱ θ)
  πepi θ = p , pepi
    where

    open Setoid 𝔻[ 𝑨 ╱ θ ]    using () renaming ( sym to ≈sym ; refl to ≈refl )
    open IsHom {𝑨 = (𝑨 ╱ θ)}  using ( compatible )
    open IsEpi

    p : 𝔻[ 𝑨 ] ⟶ 𝔻[ 𝑨 ╱ θ ]
    p ⟨$⟩ x = x
    p .cong = reflexive (θ .proj₂)

    pepi : IsEpi 𝑨 (𝑨 ╱ θ) p
    pepi .isHom .compatible = ≈sym (𝒾𝒹 .proj₂ .compatible)
    pepi .isSurjective {y} = Image_∋_.eq y ≈refl
```

In may happen that we don't care about the surjectivity of `πepi`, in which
case would might prefer to work with the *homomorphic reduct* of `πepi`.
This is obtained by applying `epi-to-hom`, like so.

```agda
  πhom : (θ : Con 𝑨 ℓ) → hom 𝑨 (𝑨 ╱ θ)
  πhom θ = epi→hom 𝑨 (𝑨 ╱ θ) (πepi θ)
```

We combine the foregoing to define a function that takes 𝑆-algebras `𝑨` and `𝑩`,
and a homomorphism `h : hom 𝑨 𝑩` and returns the canonical epimorphism from `𝑨`
onto `𝑨 [ 𝑩 ]/ker h`. (Recall, the latter is the special notation we defined
above for the quotient of `𝑨` modulo the kernel of `h`.)
